hook.say: This morning: sixteen agents score 64 to 84 percent on strict CRM checks. I went back in to see what sits around that number.

findings.label: OVERSTATED
findings.headline: Grading only the reply overstates strict success
findings.detail: Response-only grading overestimates by 10.5 to 11.0 points versus checking the final record state.
findings.evidence: Response only grading overestimates strict success by 10.5 to 11.0 percentage points.
findings.say: First, grading only the reply overstates strict success by 10.5 to 11 points, according to the paper itself. Saying is not doing.

findings.label: EARLIER DATA
findings.headline: CRMArena-Pro: multi-turn CRM success, down from 58%
findings.detail: Salesforce's earlier CRM benchmark, top agents, single-turn versus multi-turn tasks.
findings.say: Second, on the earlier CRMArena-Pro, agents dropped from about 58 percent single-turn to 35 percent multi-turn, The Decoder reports.

findings.label: STRICT SCORE
findings.headline: Zapier's strict CRM-style test: best score is 51.29%
findings.detail: AutomationBench grades the end state; every scored assertion must pass. Top three scores shown.
findings.say: Third, Zapier's AutomationBench also grades the end state strictly, and its top score is 51.29 percent.

take.headline: A good reply proves very little.
take.say: My take: a chat reply proves little. Count what changed in the record, against your own rules, before you trust the agent.

sources.title: The Decoder, Salesforce's CRM benchmark finds AI agents struggle

caption:
This morning: a new benchmark shows sixteen AI agents succeed on 64 to 84 percent of strict CRM tasks. The gap between saying and doing is real.

Three more data points: grading only the reply overstates success by about 11 points. The earlier CRMArena-Pro saw multi-turn success fall to 35 percent. Zapier's strict AutomationBench tops out at 51.29 percent.

My take: a good reply proves very little. Measure what changed in the record, against your own rules.

Comment CPQ and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.
